novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism/measurement relationship, namely a “shared, language-agnostic difficulty estimate” separated from a “language-conditioned reasoning EFFORT BUDGET,” with the same model potentially “OVERTHINK[ing]” in some languages and “UNDERTHINK[ing]” in others; this is more than a new setting or a renaming of activation steering. The closest work found was “Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Across Languages” (2025), located using searches such as “multilingual reasoning length language-specific failure,” “cross-lingual chain-of-thought inference efficiency,” and “language-conditioned stopping budget”; it reports cross-language CoT and efficiency disparities but does not posit or isolate a signed, causally steerable stopping budget decoupled from shared difficulty. Thus the step from that work to this claim requires a new core relationship rather than a direct transfer, although the proposed activation steering and length controls are standard intervention tools, supporting high but not paradigm-level novelty.
